newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HKFE membership plan sets stage for HIBOR futures.
newsitem.headline: HKFE membership plan sets stage for HIBOR futures.

text.p: The Hong Kong Futures Exchange Ltd (HKFE) is a step closer to relaunching interest rate futures trading after members approved a new membership scheme, senior exchange executives said on Tuesday.

"The exchange has been exploring the development of various Hong Kong-dollar denominated debt products and other new products," said HKFE chief executive Ivers Riley following an extraordinary meeting of members.

The exchange hoped to have all preparations completed and regulatory approval to relaunch trading in three- and six-month HIBOR (Hong Kong interbank offered rate) futures before the end of June, Riley said.

The new membership scheme allows market makers of new non-equity related products to become non-voting members of the exchange and assist in the diversification and development of the exchange, senior executives said.
"The new membership scheme may ultimately be used to facilitate the exchange's strategy of diversifying away from equity-related derivatives products," said Riley.
The new lower-priced memberships will only allow holders to trade in equity-related products such as the popular Hang Seng Index futures and options, he said.
That is, they will be restricted to prospective market makers of Hong Kong dollar-denominated debt derivative products and other new products.

"I would like to emphasise that the scheme will facilitate the exchange's development of new products for existing members to conduct customer business without infringing any of their rights," said Riley.

Riley said a "strong majority" of exchange members voted to amend the exchange company's constitution to set aside a maximum of 500 new non-voting shares for allocation to applicants as prospective market makers under the new membership scheme.

Exchange officials said they anticipated approving between five and 10 market makers applications and would not commission more than 20 under the current scheme. The HK$10,000 shares were non-transferable.
The new non-voting members, under the category of merchant trader, would be allowed to trade only for their own accounts as market makers, and not for clients.
The new members were not entitled to vote at any general meeting of the exchange. -- Kathleen Kearney (852) 2843 6933
